phases.name: Foundation
phases.goal: Data model, pilot pipeline and screens

phases.name: Availability
phases.goal: Availability per machine and planned stops

phases.name: OEE roll-up
phases.goal: Machine, line and site OEE live in Optix

activities.name: Data model and documentation
activities.definition: ISA-95 schemas for master data, history and execution, documented in four volumes.

log.text: Volumes 1 to 4 published to the project library.
Every table documented with purpose, keys and sample rows.

activities.name: Machine state pipeline, pilot
activities.definition: Land mapped tags every minute and build machine state timelines and stop events.

log.text: Running every minute on one mapped tag.
Only mapped tags are staged, to keep volume low.

activities.name: Operator screens design
activities.definition: Main view, lines and machines, orders, events and losses, assets.

activities.name: Shifts and calendar
activities.definition: Shifts stored in UTC, entered and shown in local time. Non-working days per site. Shifts generated for the next days.

log.text: Conversion approach validated against the site time zone.
No OEE outside a scheduled shift.

activities.name: Slow and no-data events
activities.definition: Slow running becomes a performance event. A gap in machine data becomes a No data stop, counted as unplanned.

log.text: Operators can reclassify a No data stop.

activities.name: Recalculation queue
activities.definition: Late data, new reasons or order changes queue the affected hours for recalculation.

activities.name: Availability by machine
activities.definition: Hourly and shift availability per machine from stop events.

activities.name: Planned stops
activities.definition: Plans as a time budget per shift, linked by hand from a filtered list.

activities.name: Part counter feed
activities.definition: Good, scrap and rework counters as deltas, safe across resets.

activities.name: PLC validation log
activities.definition: Compare runtime and downtime from events with PLC counters, for the team only.

activities.name: Routes and production orders
activities.definition: Excel import, line selection, start, hold and complete from Optix.

activities.name: Machine OEE
activities.definition: Availability, performance and quality per machine by hour, shift and order.

activities.name: Line and site OEE
activities.definition: Roll-up rules from machine to line to site.

activities.name: Live OEE for Optix
activities.definition: Current shift OEE served to the screens every minute.

questions.question: Which availability formula do we use?
questions.answer: Runtime divided by runtime plus unplanned downtime.

questions.question: Where does downtime come from: stop events or PLC counters?
questions.answer: Stop events only; PLC runtime counters are used to validate.

questions.question: How do we count time without machine data?
questions.answer: As unplanned downtime until someone explains it.

questions.question: Who sets the reason for a stop?
questions.answer: Stops start as Unknown; the operator’s reason wins.

questions.question: Is a planned stop a fixed slot or a time budget?
questions.answer: A time budget; anything beyond it is unplanned.

questions.question: Until when can an operator change a stop reason?
questions.answer: Until the end of the shift’s local day.

questions.question: How do production orders arrive?
questions.answer: From Excel as Released; started and closed in Optix.

questions.question: Which time zone name does the database use?
questions.answer: Windows name: SA Pacific Standard Time. Shifts stored in UTC, shown in local time.

questions.question: Split a slow-then-faulted episode into two events?
When does a gap in machine data become a No data stop? Proposal: after three times the tag’s log interval.
Can a planned reason be used when no plan exists? Proposal: only flagged reasons, with an optional cap.
How is line OEE built from machine results? Proposal: availability of the last machine, performance of the bottleneck, quality of all.
Does any line have machines in parallel? Proposal: treat every line as series for now.
What happens to an imported order never assigned to a line? Proposal: it stays Released and cannot start.
Line with no running order. Proposal: default machine order and cycle per line.
Line machine not in the order’s route. Proposal: excluded from line OEE for that order.
Where to log PLC validation. Proposal: validation table plus an ETL log line.
Link route steps to recipe steps. Proposal: by sequence number for now.
Non-working days. Proposal: calendar table per site.

architecture.name: Machine controllers
architecture.linkFull: EtherNet/IP, read by the edge layer
architecture.detail: Each controller already knows whether its machine is running, slow or faulted, and counts good, scrap and rework parts. Nothing is reprogrammed: the MES only reads.

architecture.name: Optix and Node-RED
architecture.detail: Reads the controller tags and publishes them with a timestamp. The tag path carries the plant hierarchy: site, area, line, cell and machine.

architecture.name: Time-series store
architecture.linkFull: Flux queries from the pipeline, filtered to mapped tags
architecture.detail: Keeps every signal with its time. It is the plant’s raw memory and never interprets anything.

architecture.name: Data pipeline
architecture.linkFull: ODBC into SQL Server staging, then stored procedures
architecture.detail: Runs every minute on its own server. Pulls only mapped tags since the last watermark, lands them raw and asks the database to transform them. A new tag is a configuration row, not new code.

architecture.name: MES database
architecture.linkFull: Stored procedures called by the screens
architecture.detail: Where signals become facts: machine timelines, stop events, counts, orders, shifts and OEE by machine, line and site. Every business rule lives here, in one place.

architecture.name: Operator screens
architecture.linkFull: Writes stop reasons and order actions back to the MES
architecture.detail: Operators start and pause orders and give every stop its reason. Managers follow OEE by hour, shift and order.
